title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this page and its neighbours. G is a GL_2-type group and SG is its SL_2-type subgroup. M_{ρ,σ} is a group equipped with Θ : M_{ρ,σ} → G. Two facts are used:
- Θ restricted to the subgroup G^+_{ρ,σ} = SG is the inclusion SG ⊂ G.
- R_{ρ,σ} is a one-dimensional torus-like group with R ∩ SG = μ_2.

Step 1, presentation (9). Grothendieck writes M_{ρ,σ} as a quotient: M ≅ \tilde M/μ_2, where \tilde M = R_{ρ,σ} × SG and μ_2 is embedded diagonally. This is the analogue of GL_2 ≅ (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2.

Step 2, the maps. κ : R → G_m is the restriction of Θ to R, which acts by scalars. T_0 ⊂ G is a rank-one torus with T_0 ∩ SG = 1, so det|T_0 : T_0 → G_m is an isomorphism, and i_{T_0} is its inverse (10). A typical example is T_0 = {diag(t,1)}.

Step 3, Θ on \tilde M. For a point (r, u_0) of \tilde M one has Θ(r, u_0) = κ(r)u_0, whose determinant is κ(r)^2.

Step 4, the subgroup M(0). On the previous page M_{ρ,σ}(0) := Θ^{-1}(T_0) was introduced and shown to be a subgroup-section of M → Γ_{ρ,σ}. Here it is computed explicitly. The condition Θ(r, u_0) ∈ T_0 forces κ(r)u_0 = i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2), hence (11):
 u_0 = κ(r)^{-1} i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2).
So the inverse image of M(0) in \tilde M is the graph (12) of the map (13):
 φ°_0(r) = κ(r)^{-1} i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2), φ°_0 : R → SG.

Step 5, checks. φ°_0 is a homomorphism, because κ(r) is a central scalar and i_{T_0} is a homomorphism. Its determinant is κ^{-2}κ^2 = 1, so it lands in SG. On μ_2 one has κ(r) = r = ±1, so i_{T_0}(1) = 1 and φ°_0(r) = r^{-1} = r. This is exactly the compatibility condition (6), φ°|μ_2 = id, required on the previous page for sections. In the example T_0 = diag(t,1), φ°_0(r) = diag(κ, κ^{-1}).

Step 6, the remark. The page ends with a Remark, continued on the next page: to define this section it suffices to choose any rank-one torus T_0 and set (13). The next page enlarges M(0) to M[0] = Θ^{-1}(B'_0), with B'_0 = T_0·L_0, a semidirect product.

Purpose. This is part of classifying the sections M(0), M(1/2), M(−j) that enter Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' computations, i.e. splittings of an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ}. Each section is encoded by a homomorphism R → SG restricting to the identity on μ_2.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Θ(r,u_0) ∈ T_0 indeed gives u_0 = κ^{-1}i_{T_0}(κ^2), and this map is a homomorphism into SG that is the identity on μ_2.
Notational slips in the manuscript itself: M_{φ,σ} is written for M_{ρ,σ}, and the final line writes φ°_0(r) = κ(r)^{-1} = κ(r) = r. The latter is fine on μ_2 because κ|μ_2 is the identity inclusion.

ideas.what: Presentation of M_{ρ,σ} as (R_{ρ,σ} × SG)/μ_2 with μ_2 embedded diagonally
Explicit section of M → Γ obtained as Θ^{-1}(T_0) for a rank-one torus T_0 mapped isomorphically by det; it is encoded by the homomorphism φ°_0(r) = κ(r)^{-1} i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2) into SL_2
ideas.modern_name: splitting of a central extension by a complementary torus

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine explicit computation inside Grothendieck's case-by-case analysis of sections. It is correct and elementary, and contains no new idea beyond standard linear algebraic group manipulations.
transcription_corrections: (12) should read (r, κ(r)^{-1} i_{T_0}(κ(r)^2)). The square applies to κ(r) inside i_{T_0}, not to i_{T_0}(κ(r)).
The marginal note likely reads: 'κ : R_{ρ,σ} → G_m l'homomorphisme canonique, par restriction d'extension [?] Θ|R_{ρ,σ}'.
'dire que c'est ∈ U signifie donc' likely reads 'dire que c'est ∈ T_0 signifie donc'.
'en d'autres termes cela correspond à une ... pour une section, une' likely reads 'en d'autres termes cela correspond, au niveau des sections, à'.

'Comme il se doit, c'est bien un homomorphisme' is correct. 'et se réduit sur μ_2 à l'identité' likely reads 'et se réduit sur μ_2 à l'identité, car κ(r)^2 = 1 et on a φ°_0(r) = κ(r)^{-1} = κ(r) = r'.
The crossed-out text reads 'Avant de quitter [?]', and the remark begins 'Pour définir cette section, il suffisait'.
